Results.ReviewText: Overall a high quality grill.  It is quick to light and has very nice even heat distribution on the flames.  I don't notice any major hotspots or cold spots.  The heavy duty cast iron grilling surface is also nice.  And it appears to be made of high quality construction that should last a long time.  the only complaint I have is that the flames are so far from the grill surface, and are shielded by the "flavorizer bars" that is is harder to get a nice caramelized sear on meat.  Even though the grill can (eventually) get up to 600 degrees, not enough to sear, the sear is most in the grill marks, presumably since the cooking surface is a hair to far above the flames.  For such a high price point, I was expecting a bit more. But overall I am happy with it.

Results.ReviewText:
Bought the Spirit II E-310 to replace my 14 (or so) year old Weber Performer charcoal grill and after the first couple of grills, am left wondering why I hadn't made the switch years ago.  Loved my Performer (although it kinda morphed into a bit of a love-hate relationship when its gas charcoal lighting system  stopped working a couple years ago), but am certainly happy with my purchase decision.  The grill is solid, well designed, and above all else--works well!  Switching from charcoal to gas, I knew I would be giving up some of that smoky flavor, but now that my grates are starting to get a good season on them, the results have been awesome.

Quick note on assembly....as I unpacked the grill (and its many parts) from the box, I was thinking that I would be in for a pretty unpleasant experience, but the BILT app that you can download for step by step 3-D instructions made it a pretty stress free assembly.  Being able to zoom in on parts, joints, fasteners, etc, made assembly pretty simple.  Still took me an hour and a half or two (was taking my time not to over torque any fasteners or scratch any finishes), but everything came together easily and worked great from the start.

Overall, very happy with purchase and would definitely recommend!
Results.Title: Well built.  Easy Assembly.  Great results!

ClientResponses.Response:
Hello, we are sorry to hear about this issue. It sounds like you may be activating a safety device built into the regulator.To ensure that you are not inadvertently activating the safety device as you turn on the grill, please use the following procedure:

-Turn all burner control knobs to OFF, including the side burner control knob if present.

-Make sure the grill lid is open. Open the LP tank valve and then wait at least 60 seconds. This will allow the hose and regulator to pressurize.

-Turn the appropriate burner control knob for your model grill to the START/HIGH position and then ignite the grill by pushing the ignition button.

-Turn each of the other burner control knobs to high, one at a time, and press the igniter button (if applicable for your model). Repeat this process until all the burners have been lit.

-Close the grill lid.

-The grill should reach approximately 500 to 550 degrees in 10-15 minutes.

If you continue to experience an issue please contact our support team. We will be glad  to help further. Thanks!

Results.ReviewText:
So far after finally getting the grill put together (had to wait for parts from Weber that came in the box broken), I did the directions and "cured" the grill for first use.  Temp went up past 500 degrees which was good.  When I went to grill the first two times, the grill came on and I set all burners to high to preheat.  Went out to put my meat on and reset the burners to medium and the temp had decreased to 200 degrees both times. Both times I shut down the gas and turned off the grill (we have had weber gas grills for decades 
now) and restarted the grill.  Both times it went back up to 500 degrees.  Just irritating that it isn't staying on the first time we light it.
